conceptFirstReview.scope: Concept-first editorial changes and formula classification for all 44 active lessons; all 74 questions (key, every distractor, worked example) reviewed; retained maths recomputed; 5 retained Python listings executed; 8 new analogies reviewed; changed/added glossary entries (diode, full-speed-usb) verified, others spot-checked. summary.countingMethod: claimsChecked counts complete review groups, not atomic claims: 44 lesson bodies + 74 full questions + 16 retained formula cards (15 lesson, 1 question) + 5 executed Python listings + 8 added analogies + 2 glossary entries (diode, full-speed-usb) = 149. numericalRecomputations (81) counts individual values recomputed in evidence/cf2-synth-midi-verifier/recompute.json. errorsCorrected counts factual/teaching errors fixed; editorialFixes counts wording/typo fixes; hedgedOrRemoved counts hedges added. corrections: midi-synth-handling-controller-curves analogy: 'every key is the same width … equal physical steps' was inaccurate (white and black keys differ; a piano's semitone steps are not equal-width) → 'moving up one key, white or black, raises the pitch by the same semitone' and 'each step up is the same frequency ratio'.

midi-fundamentals-q6: timing 'first and last edge' of a Note On can span only 29 bit-times (about 0.93 ms) when the stop bit follows a 0, so it did not match the 30-bit explanation → prompt now times from the start of the first start bit to the end of the last stop bit.
Glossary diode: 'the LED never sees a damaging reverse voltage' was absolute → the reverse-connected diode holds the LED's reverse voltage to about one diode forward drop.
midi-hardware-q1 worked example: garbled 'along the socket rim around the socket' → 'do not run in numeric order around the socket rim' (editorial).
midi-studio-integration-q7 option 1: typo 'Choose a one tempo sender' → 'Choose one tempo sender' (editorial).

Hedged: midi-synth-handling-controller-curves: ratio perception of filter cutoffs and envelope times reframed as a widely used design rule of thumb, not an exact perceptual law (lesson text, takeaway and q7 worked example).
Hedged: midi-hardware-usb-event-packets: 'many event packets per millisecond' now gives the 12 Mbit/s full-speed figure and states that throughput depends on device, host scheduling and driver.
Hedged: midi-fundamentals-q12: USB chord spread now 'usually much less', timing depending on device, host and driver.

Hedged: midi-hardware-q5: the ≈5.3 mA prediction now states its model (nominal 3.3 V, exact resistors, fixed LED drop, cable/driver ignored) in the prompt; worked example notes real forward drop varies with current (CA-033).
Hedged: midi-messages-q8: recompute-on-range-change assumption made explicit in the prompt; worked example explains the alternative behaviour.
gaps: No physical MIDI or audio hardware measurements: loop currents, levels and latencies are specification or model values.
Render check at 390 px and offline view were not performed in this pass (build, renderer, diagram, formula and glossary unit tests pass).

Glossary: diode (corrected) and full-speed-usb (added) were verified against sources; the other 171 entries were spot-checked for sense and alias capture, not re-verified exhaustively. Their earlier verification is inherited.

velocity-note-end, lengths-pressure, control-change-map, rpn-bank-program, sysex-mode, midi-two-scope, parser-state, stuck-note-defences, din-loop, trs-thru and several studio lessons still have one-line key-takeaway sections; acceptable but thin.

lowConfidence.reason: Pitch-ratio perception is standard; extension to cutoff and times is a common design heuristic without a fetched psychoacoustic source. Now hedged in the text.

lowConfidence.reason: Recomputed correctly (1.4 V / 263 Ω = 5.32 mA) under stated model assumptions; real LED drop varies with current and driver low-state voltage is ignored. Not measured.

lowConfidence.claim: USB MIDI carries many event packets per millisecond; a DIN chord is much less spread over USB (also midi-fundamentals-q12).
lowConfidence.reason: 12 Mbit/s full speed is verified; actual USB MIDI throughput and timing depend on endpoint size, host polling and drivers and were not measured. Hedged.

lowConfidence.claim: Analogy limit: impedance imbalance converts common-mode interference into a difference signal; rejection is finite.
lowConfidence.reason: Supported by the IEC 60268-3 statement as cited on Wikipedia (secondary); the Jensen primary application note now returns 404.

lowConfidence.claim: Digitakt / Digitakt II ports, ratings, menus and Ableton Live 12 behaviour (all studio-integration lessons, note-frequency, usb-host-roles, sine-headroom, load-bridging, dc-coupling).
lowConfidence.reason: Re-fetched Digitakt OS 1.53 and Digitakt II OS 1.17 manuals and Live 12 manual pages on 2026-10-29 and confirmed the quoted facts, but product facts are time-sensitive and version-specific; lessons tell the reader to confirm their model and OS.

midi-fundamentals-din-wire-time.rationale: Retitled to 'Count DIN MIDI wire time' (id unchanged; title matches the framed-bit counting content). The 31,250 bit/s ±1%, 8-N-1, LSB-first and 320 µs facts match CA-033 and stay visible; one reference card keeps the message-time relationship, the duplicate byte-time card is removed. q6 now diagnoses a measured wire time (verifier tightened the timing points so 30 bit-times is exact); q12 supplies the 0.96 ms figure and tests the chord ripple (8.64 ms recomputed), with the USB comparison hedged.

questionsRewritten.midi-fundamentals-q12: Kept the chord-spread prediction but supplied the 0.96 ms per-message figure in the prompt and replaced the formula walkthrough with reasoning; corrected the vague "USB MIDI is much faster" to many event packets per millisecond. analogyReview.scope: Independently re-read all 44 active lessons with analogy disclosures closed; reviewed the 8 added analogies' mapping and limits against primary sources and recorded why the other 36 need none.

midi-fundamentals-event-audio-paths.rationale: Player-piano roll: holes = note events, piano = receiving synth; limit covers live stream, extra values (velocity, channel, controllers, clock, SysEx) and the separate audio cable. Facts stay outside the disclosure.

midi-fundamentals-din-wire-time.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Short timing fact; the chord-ripple explanation is already concrete and an analogy would add little.

midi-fundamentals-status-data-boundaries.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Bit-flag rule is a definition; the byte diagram is clearer than any analogy.

midi-fundamentals-channel-nibbles.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Off-by-one numbering is procedural; the table states it directly.

midi-fundamentals-note-frequency.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Already concrete; an analogy for exponential pitch is added in the controller-curves lesson (piano keyboard) rather than repeated here.

midi-fundamentals-velocity-note-end.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: A protocol rule; analogy would not clarify it.

midi-fundamentals-encode-decode-trace.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Byte-level procedure; code and trace are the teaching device.

midi-messages-lengths-pressure.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Reference table; no analogy needed.

midi-messages-control-change-map.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Reference table.

midi-messages-controller-pairs.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Coarse/fine pairing is already explained with concrete examples; the q7 trace tests it.

midi-messages-bend-packing.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Bit packing is shown directly by code.

midi-messages-bend-frequency.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Mapping is simple proportional reasoning; analogy would repeat the prose.

midi-messages-running-status.rationale: Ditto marks = running status buffer; limit correctly states one remembered status, cleared by SysEx/System Common, untouched by real-time bytes (spec 4.2.1 appendix).

midi-messages-clock-transport.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Clock/tempo relation is concrete; a metronome analogy would add little.

midi-messages-sysex-mode.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Protocol allocation facts.

midi-synth-handling-receive-audio-bounda.rationale: Radio studio: post-room pigeonhole = ring buffer, producer = control loop, presenter = audio callback; limit names overflow and the need for a concurrency-safe hand-over.

midi-synth-handling-parser-state.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: State-machine code and traces are the teaching device.

midi-synth-handling-mono-priority.rationale: Panel microphone: raised hands = held keys, microphone = the one voice, chair's rule = note priority; limit covers instant switching and the separate retrigger/legato choice.

midi-synth-handling-stuck-note-defences.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Checklist of failure causes.

midi-synth-handling-controller-curves.rationale: Piano keyboard: each key up (white or black) = one fixed ratio, like an exponential CC map; verifier corrected 'every key is the same width / equal physical steps'. Limit states range-dependent step size and that cutoff is not a played pitch.

midi-synth-handling-controller-smoothing.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: One-pole smoothing analogy belongs to the synthesis DSP module; repeating it would add no understanding.

midi-hardware-din-loop.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: The isolation analogy is placed in the next lesson where it explains the optocoupler; the loop diagram is clearer here.

midi-hardware-input-isolation.rationale: Torch through a window: torch = optocoupler LED, watcher = photodetector on the receiver's own supply; limit covers isolation voltage rating (not a mains safety barrier), minimum LED current and switching speed, consistent with CA-033.

midi-hardware-input-reference.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Circuit facts and the reactance table already make the point concrete.

midi-hardware-output-loop-current.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Series-circuit reasoning is explained directly; a water analogy would be generic filler.

midi-hardware-output-fault-rating.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Fault-case rating is a direct engineering check.

midi-hardware-trs-thru.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Pinout facts.

midi-hardware-usb-event-packets.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Packet layout is shown by the byte diagram.

midi-hardware-usb-host-roles.rationale: Meeting chair = USB host scheduling all transfers; two members without a chair = two devices; limit covers power, enumeration and dual-role ports.

midi-audio-levels-connection-families.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Level families are a classification table.

midi-audio-levels-voltage-references.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: The subtraction trap is explained concretely; a currency-conversion analogy was considered but would add length without new understanding.

midi-audio-levels-sine-headroom.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Short, concrete lesson.

midi-audio-levels-load-bridging.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Divider reasoning with a table is concrete; a hydraulic analogy would be generic.

midi-audio-levels-balanced-connectors.rationale: Two people in a lift: lift motion = common-mode interference, height difference = wanted signal; limit (unequal impedances convert interference into a difference; finite rejection) matches the IEC 60268-3 statement cited on Wikipedia's Balanced audio page.

midi-audio-levels-dc-coupling.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Filter behaviour is explained directly with typical values.

midi-studio-integration-connection-plan.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Planning procedure.

midi-studio-integration-monitor-latency.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Latency budget is explained as a sum of stages.

midi-studio-integration-hum-test-session.rationale: Reviewed with disclosures closed: Procedure with safety warnings; analogy could obscure the earth-safety rule.
